title: Verify and compact large artifacts locally before upload
summary: The Colab file-transfer plane is not an object store. A 480,178,064-byte recovery archive failed during upload before model work, while a locally verified compact payload of 77,062,608 bytes was successfully dispatched. The correct response was not to infer a universal Colab size limit; it was to unpack and authenticate the archive locally, remove provably redundant frozen tensors, bind the compact payload to the original digest, and upload only what the worker needed.
evidence_note: Live Gemma dev20/dev21 regrade incident: monolithic ~480 MB upload failed; compact ~73.5 MiB payload succeeded. PEFT had saved two redundant resized F32 embedding/lm-head tensors. No universal threshold is claimed.
invariants: Do not infer a provider-wide maximum upload size from one failed transfer.
Prefer small immutable digest-bound inputs over monolithic convenience archives.
Compaction must be fail-closed: prove removed bytes are reconstructible/redundant before deleting them.
Bind compact artifacts to the original artifact identity so transformation is auditable.
